case_analysis.thread_summary: The thread concerns qualification planning for a new Bluetooth keyboard family and the scope of Bluetooth SIG qualification testing. The customer initially explored whether qualification could be completed using only core-layer registration, then decided to include profile qualification because the product implements HID over GATT Profile (HOGP). The discussion covers quotation updates, required profile testing, qualification scheduling, representative model selection, and collection of qualification inputs such as ICS data and product information. Internal follow-up focuses on preparing PTS testing and selecting a single representative Bluetooth model from a multi-model product family.
case_analysis.key_technical_discussion: A key topic is the distinction between obtaining a Bluetooth qualification entry based only on required core layers versus qualifying a product as an HOGP-enabled HID device. The consultant explains that an HID keyboard implementing HOGP should undergo profile qualification rather than relying solely on core-layer registration. The thread highlights that under the newer qualification process, HOGP qualification also pulls in related profile requirements such as BAS, DIS, and HIDS, at least for their mandatory functionality. Preparation for PTS testing requires collection of HOGP ICS information, review of any feature changes from a previously qualified design, and creation of an appropriate test plan. The discussion also confirms that a representative model can be selected for Bluetooth testing within a multi-variant keyboard family.
case_analysis.key_decision_logic: The central reasoning is that qualification scope must match the Bluetooth functionality actually implemented and marketed. While a product may be registrable using only the minimum required core layers, that approach does not qualify the product as an HOGP-enabled keyboard. Because the product is a Bluetooth HID device and the customer wants qualification coverage consistent with the implemented functionality, HOGP profile qualification and its dependent profile requirements are included. Representative-model testing is acceptable for the product family provided the customer identifies the model used as the qualification representative.
case_analysis.risk_if_done_wrong: If the product is registered using only core-layer qualification while implementing and promoting HOGP functionality, the resulting qualification may not accurately cover the product's claimed Bluetooth capabilities. Failing to identify required dependent profiles, collect correct ICS information, or define the proper test scope could lead to incomplete test planning, qualification rework, additional testing effort, and schedule delays. Delayed submission of ICS information can also postpone test-plan generation and profile testing activities.
case_analysis.consulting_mistake: The initial quotation omitted HOGP profile testing because the BLE profile field in the qualification request documentation was left blank. This created the impression that testing might not be required. The issue was corrected by clarifying the implemented HOGP functionality, explaining the qualification implications, and issuing a revised scope that included the required profile testing and related dependencies.
case_analysis.consulting_takeaway: Always determine qualification scope from the Bluetooth features actually implemented and intended for qualification, not solely from request forms or legacy assumptions. For Bluetooth HID products, verify HOGP support early, review ICS data against previously qualified designs, identify dependent profile requirements, and confirm whether representative-model qualification can be used before building the test plan and quotation.
